st: Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Put it in a large pot with the onion, garlic and [[2 cups]] water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the smoked fish and the whole Scotch bonnet. Do not cut it unless you want fiery heat.
Pour the palm nut cream into a bowl and stir in [[2 cups]] hot water from the pot to loosen it, then pour it back into the pot.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, for 40 minutes. The soup will thicken and the red oil will rise to the top.
Check that the chicken has reached 165°F (74°C). Taste and add up to [[0.5 tsp]] more salt.
Remove the pepper. Serve the soup over hot rice.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the black pepper. Blend the tomatoes, bell pepper, chopped onion and chili into a smooth puree.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot and brown the chicken for 8 minutes. Remove it and set aside.
Fry the sliced onion in the same pot for 4 minutes, add [[3 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1 tbsp]] curry powder and [[1 tsp]] thyme and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the blended puree and cook, stirring, for 15 minutes until thick and the oil separates at the edges.
Add [[4 cups]] chicken broth and [[1 tsp]] salt and bring to a boil. Return the chicken to the pot.
Stir in [[3 cups]] rinsed rice, cover tightly with foil and a lid, and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes.
Check the chicken reached 165°F (74°C) and the rice is tender. If not, add a splash of water and cook 5 minutes more.
Fluff gently with a fork and serve hot.
Wash the leaves well and chop them finely. Remove any tough stems.
Put the chicken in a pot with [[2 cups]] water, half the onion, the garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Add the smoked fish and the Scotch bonnet and simmer 5 minutes.
In a second pot heat [[0.25 cup]] palm oil over medium heat and cook the remaining onion for 4 minutes.
Add the chopped leaves to the oil in handfuls, stirring until they wilt.
Pour the chicken, fish and broth into the greens. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are very soft.
Make sure the chicken is at 165°F (74°C). Taste and add up to [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Serve over rice.
If using frozen cassava leaves, thaw and drain them. Chop finely or pulse a few times in a food processor.
Put the leaves in a pot with [[3 cups]] water and boil for 20 minutes to soften. Do not drain.
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Heat [[0.33 cup]] palm oil in another pot and brown the chicken for 8 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook 4 minutes.
Pour the leaves and their liquid over the chicken. Add the smoked fish and the whole Scotch bonnet.
Cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until the leaves are dark and the oil rises.
Check the chicken reached 165°F (74°C), taste and add [[0.5 tsp]] salt if needed, then serve with rice.
Peel the cassava, cut out the woody core in the center and cut the flesh into chunks.
Put the chunks in a pot with [[6 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Boil for 25 minutes until very soft.
Drain, keeping about half a cup of the cooking water.
Mash the cassava in a large bowl with a heavy potato masher, or pound it in a sturdy bowl with a wooden pestle, for 8 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Add a spoon of the reserved water if the dough is too stiff to work.
With wet hands, shape the fufu into four smooth balls.
Warm [[3 tbsp]] palm oil in a small pan, cook the onion and chili for 3 minutes and spoon over the fufu or serve alongside.
Serve warm with soup or stew.

st: Rinse the goat meat and put it in a large pot with the onion, garlic, ginger and [[8 cups]] water.
Bring to a boil and skim off the foam from the top.
Add [[1 tbsp]] pepper soup spice, [[2 tsp]] salt and the Scotch bonnet peppers.
Cover and simmer on medium-low for 1 hour 15 minutes until the goat is tender. Goat is tough, so do not rush this.
Add the smoked fish if using and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the basil or scent leaves, cook 2 minutes more, then taste and add salt or pepper.
Ladle into bowls, careful with the hot peppers, and serve piping hot.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a loaf pan with a little oil.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until almost smooth.
Whisk in [[0.5 cup]] sugar, the eggs, [[0.25 cup]] oil and [[0.25 cup]] milk.
In another bowl mix [[2 cups]] rice flour, [[2 tsp]] baking powder, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Stir the dry mix into the wet mix until just combined. The batter will be thick.
Scrape into the pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 50 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out and slice when cooler.
In a large bowl mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sugar, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Add about [[1.25 cups]] warm water and stir into a thick, sticky batter.
Beat the batter with a wooden spoon for 2 minutes until smooth.
Cover and leave in a warm spot for 1 hour until puffy and doubled.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Wet two spoons. Scoop a spoonful of batter and drop it in the oil, frying 4 or 5 at a time.
Fry for 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, plain or dusted with sugar.
